subject: Polaris Health — capacity absorption profile & tail-latency stress test
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Polaris Health — initial absorption profile & quick ask

Hi Olivia,

Great speaking earlier. Per our call I ran a compact absorption model for the three phased rollout you described (seed users -> beta -> full prod). High level findings attached (polaris_absorption_model_v1.xlsx). Key bullet highlights below so you can share with your SRE/procurement folks: 

- Typical steady-state traffic (phase 1 beta): ~2.2M tokens/day (~25 tps sustained, ~500k tokens/hour).
- Projected peak windows (phase 3 full prod): short bursts to ~65k tokens/sec for 60–120s, and sustained 6–9k tokens/sec during business-hours peak.
- SLO target discussed: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms, with P99 tail <= 800ms.
- Model variant planned: open-llm-caster-12B (quantized) — single-GPU throughput (steady) baseline ~1,800 tokens/sec for 1024-context; burst optimized setup with batching pushes to ~3,200 tokens/sec per GPU before latency degradation.

Immediate asks: could your SRE confirm whether burst windows are typically concurrent across regions or localized? That will change how much headroom we recommend. Also best to have procurement confirm if a monthly reserved slab is acceptable (we can map to a commit that gives 20–30% effective unit-cost savings).

I attached: polaris_absorption_model_v1.xlsx (workbook with token-flow, per-route TPS, and latency-sensitivity curves). I also included a quick “ops play” page with fallback model variants if you need to trade cost for latency.

Next steps: if SRE can confirm burst concurrency by EOD Tuesday we’ll finalize the GPU-slab ask and a recommended burst buffer (numbers below).

Numbers we expect to propose (draft):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 x L40-like GPUs (estimated steady absorption + 20% cushion for organic growth).
- Burst buffer: additional 4 gpus (on-demand / reserved-burst) to cover short 60–120s spikes to 65k tokens/sec while staying within P95 latency of 300ms.
- Estimated blended p95 latency under proposed config: ~260ms.

Thanks —
Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the notes, Olivia — quick answers and an ops-safe sizing baked from our internal stress runs: 

- The 65k tokens/sec spike in Mina's workbook is a global total (both regions combined). Given your SRE note that bursts are correlated across east/west, we should assume that the worst-case is a near-global spike.

- Model throughput assumptions (measured on our benchmark rig at 1024 context, quantized profile):
  * open-llm-caster-12B (quantized) — steady throughput: 1.8k tokens/sec/GPU (P50).
  * For micro-batched burst mode (lower batching latency), we see 3.1k tokens/sec/GPU before P95 starts to climb.
  * Tail behavior: P99 degrades ~2.5–3x vs P95 under sustained heavy load unless KV cache and prefix caching warmups are used.

- Sizing recommendation (ops-safe) to meet your SLOs (P95 <= 300ms, P99 <= 900ms) given correlated bursts: 
  1) Reserved slab: 10 GPUs (L40-equivalent). This covers the sustained 6–9k tokens/sec peak with ~25–30% headroom for organic growth and warm cache effects.
  2) Burst layer: 6 GPUs (hot spares / burst-on-demand) to absorb an immediate 60–120s spike up to 65k tokens/sec. The blended capacity (reserved + burst) yields ~49k tokens/sec conservative estimate; we achieve 65k tokens/sec only if we accept higher batching/latency risk.
  3) Operational mitigations: enable aggressive prefix KV caching on high-frequency routes and a short-term model-fallback (caster-7B) that can handle extreme bursts with degraded quality but sub-400ms P95.

- Expected latencies (modeled):
  * With proposed reserved slab alone under sustained 9k tokens/sec: P95 ~270ms, P99 ~810ms.
  * During a 65k global spike with burst layer available: P95 ~320–400ms depending on cache warmness, P99 ~1.2s — this is outside your stated P99 target. The fallback model keeps p95 < 400ms and p99 ~850–950ms but at lower output quality.

Attachments: I ran the tail-latency stress harness and exported results (tail_latency_stress_results_v2.pdf). Please review page 2 for percentile breakdowns and page 5 for the readiness checklist (KV cache thresholds, batching caps).

Action items I recommend:
- Polaris SRE: confirm whether automatic cache warming is feasible for the first 5 minutes of the window (that materially reduces p99).
- Procurement: let us know if you can convert 2–3 burst GPUs to reserved-with-burst pricing to lower on-demand risk.
- Mina/Jordan: I'll hand this to ops to draft a formal SLA exception if Polaris needs hard P99 <= 900ms during global spikes.

-Karthik
Director, Inference Solutions
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: tail_latency_stress_results_v2.pdf)

Subject: Re: Polaris Health — capacity absorption profile & tail-latency stress test (next steps)

Olivia — thanks for the quick turn. Two pragmatic options that match your risk tolerance: 

Option A (latency-first, higher cost):
- Reserved: 12 GPUs
- Burst-on-demand: 4 GPUs (for rare >75k spikes)
- Rationale: pushes P95 comfortable under 300ms and keeps P99 closer to 900ms even under correlated peaks with cache warming.

Option B (cost-first, graceful degradation):
- Reserved: 8 GPUs
- Burst: 6 GPUs (on-demand) + fallback model caster-7B enabled for >50k spikes
- Rationale: keeps committed cost lower; in extreme spikes quality degrades but latency targets for P95 remain near 300–400ms and P99 mostly within ~1s (with fallback).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Polaris SRE to confirm cache-warm capability and whether bursts are fully concurrent across both regions (deadline: 2027-08-12 EOD).
2) Procurement: indicate whether converting 2 burst GPUs to reserved-with-burst is feasible (we can show TCO tradeoffs).
3) I’ll prepare a formal commitment proposal mapping Option A/B to monthly slab SKUs and a short-run SLA exception draft if you need hard P99 language.

If that sounds right I can send a one-pager and a DocuSign term sheet to speed procurement.

—Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachments referenced: polaris_absorption_model_v1.xlsx; tail_latency_stress_results_v2.pdf)
